correctness.rationale: The source circular word W=0^a(10)^(k-1)1 has k zero and k one runs, one zero run of length a, all others length one. Exactly two distinct position deletions partition into disjoint cases by number s of deleted ones (recoverable from remaining one count). For s=0, two long-run zeros / one long and one singleton / two singleton runs yield 1+(k-1)+C(k-1,2)=1+C(k,2) distinct necklaces. For s=1, the adjacent-to-long-run cases coalesce to one, interior one deleted after long-run-zero deletion yields H_a(k)=k-2 if a>=4 and ceil((k-2)/2) if a=3 due to interchange of equal-length two-zero runs, and other cases yield (k-2)^2. For s=2, deletion of ones neighboring the long run gives k-2 classes, internal pairs yield C(k-2,2), with floor((k-3)/2) duplicate signatures exactly at a=3 when two zero runs of length three interchange. The case disjointness and oriented *cyclic* signatures (no reversal quotient) yield the T_s formulas and totals 2k²-6k+8 if a=3 versus 2k²-5k+5 if a>=4; gap k-3 begins k=4. Independently built a canonical least-rotation necklace enumeration from every unordered deleted-position pair and confirmed all three counts for 168 parameter pairs (a=3..8,k=3..30). Finite tests corroborate, not replace, all-a,k run-signature exhaustion.
